_comment: BASELINE Radar live-run profile ('default') — the canonical record of how the Worker runs a live measurement. The scheduled run and run-radar.ps1 load this as the base; every other profile is an overlay carrying ONLY its delta. run-radar.ps1 supplies machine-specific values at runtime (output directories, the SEC User-Agent); SECRETS are never written here: the hosted reader's API key comes from the environment variable NAMED by Radar:Ai:OpenAi:ApiKeyEnvVar (DEEPINFRA_API_KEY); only the NAME lives here. STANDING FACTS ONLY (spec 213): every value this comment once quoted has an owner — read the owner, never a number in prose. Live/unit fingerprint pins: ScoringConfigFingerprintTests (each window is its own correct answer — never reconcile them; check a run's stamp against the pair for the window it used). Formula set: ScoreFormulaVersions.All. Extractor rule set: KeywordSignalExtractor.RuleSetVersion. Strategy count, order and indices: the Strategies array below (count it; never trust an index quoted in prose). Universe size and per-source feed coverage: data/companies.json. Operating calls, Lead arm and review dates: data/strategy-operating-calls.json + docs/strategy-lifecycle.md. Per-spec decisions and every historical pin: docs/architecture-history.md ('default.json _comment history'). RunProfileCommentGuardTests enforces this. OPERATOR RULES (not derivable from code): (a) a NAMED strategy is immutable by convention — a retune is a NEW name; editing one in place trips StrategyIdentityGuard; a guard halt after a DELIBERATE identity move is CORRECT — consciously delete or re-record data/scoring-configs/strategies/{name}.json (git-ignored; never fabricated) and check the first run's stamp against ScoringConfigFingerprintTests. (b) An overlay that changes WEIGHTS must re-point Strategies[0].ScoringProfile — overlaying Radar:Scoring:Profile alone FAILS OPEN (DefaultRunProfileTests is the guard). (c) The three baseline- comparators (baseline-earnings-only, baseline-activity-only, baseline-media-only) must be IDENTICAL in a baseline run and an experiment — a control exists to be beaten. (d) ReportMaxItems, Ai:MaxFilingsPerRun and Labels are operational/display parameters, NOT fingerprint inputs (the cap's rule is below). (e) The 2026-09-29 precommitted claim boundary is immutable by convention (owners: Radar:Efficacy:Comparison below and appsettings.json). WHY EACH NON-DEFAULT VALUE IS SET: ReportMaxItems=120 — each strategy section renders only the top N, so scored companies past the cap never reach the reader; the Worker refuses to start when this is below the seeded universe size, so a universe expansion must raise it in the same change (deliberately NOT derived from the universe: a cap that tracks the universe is no cap). Ai:MaxFilingsPerRun=50 — the code default is a stale pre-pacer cost limiter; SecRequestPacer owns SEC fair-access protection, so this is a cost knob, not a safety one. Prices.Enabled=true — acquires price history as validation/reference data OUTSIDE the pipeline (AD-14) so score-vs-price efficacy can be read; price never enters scoring. Efficacy.Enabled=true — turns on the read-only score-vs-price render and the strategy leaderboard (AD-14 read side), which ranks strategies against price. Ai:Filings:PersistReadDebug=true — diagnostics-only per-read JSON (git-ignored, not a fingerprint input) so marker hit rates accrue from live runs and prompt-phrase changes are argued from data. News:RecencyWindowDays=7 — declared explicitly so this file RECORDS the news-attention posture rather than inheriting it and an overlay cannot silently restore the unfiltered feed; a hashed identity input (see Radar:News:_comment). disclosure-led-v11 Labels {Investigate 20, Watch 15} — the Lead arm's label lines are per-strategy config — fixed triage prevalence, connected to no outcome (scripts/audit-label-thresholds.ps1 reproduces it); every effective Lead must declare them or the Worker refuses to build the report.

News._comment: Radar:News:RecencyWindowDays — the Google News RSS news-attention collector's recency window, declared EXPLICITLY here (matching the code default and appsettings.json) so this profile RECORDS the posture it runs rather than inheriting it, and so an experiment overlay that redeclares Radar:News cannot silently restore the unfiltered feed. It appends a 'when:{n}d' term to the search phrase. 0 disables it and reproduces the unfiltered URL byte-for-byte; a negative value fails startup naming this key. A company's FIRST collection stays unfiltered — decided from the persisted observation archive, never from a clock — so seeding still acquires back history. IT IS A HASHED ScoringConfigVersion INPUT (NewsQueryScoringIdentity, the newsquery= segment): changing it is a scoring-identity move. The current live and unit stamps are owned by ScoringConfigFingerprintTests — never a value quoted in prose — and after a deliberate move the operator step is to delete or re-record every configured data/scoring-configs/strategies/{name}.json (git-ignored, never fabricated); StrategyIdentityGuard halting before collection until that is done is correct. MaxRecordsPerCompany, the absolute parse ceiling, the request count and the pacing are separate knobs this value does not touch, and Radar:Gdelt:MaxRecordsPerCompany is a DIFFERENT collector's knob. History (the live measurement behind the window and the pins it once quoted): docs/architecture-history.md, 'default.json _comment history' (spec 213).

NewsResearch._comment: SPEC 177 (2026-08-22) - point-in-time news observation archive. CaptureRss=true (also the code default, declared here so the baseline's posture is explicit): every relevance-kept Google News RSS article is archived immutably under <outRoot>/news-observations (run-radar.ps1 supplies Radar:NewsResearch:ObservationDirectory) with its exact bounded <description> payload, publisher provenance and retrieval instant, plus a per-run batch manifest tied to the PipelineRunRecord by explicit batch id. Capture is independent of AI, is never evidence, never a signal, never a scoring/fingerprint input, and no existing news evidence/signal/score moves. The safe ArticleFetch seam stays SHIPPED-DISABLED with an empty allowlist (enabling it requires a non-empty domain allowlist + contact-bearing User-Agent, and fails startup otherwise); the one-shot migration (run-radar.ps1 -MigrateNewsObservations) is never part of this baseline run. SPEC 179 (2026-08-22) - the in-process news-risk SHADOW read is enabled below: after each unfiltered full run, the top live Research-strategy leaders (5 per arm, deduped, max 30) get a cited thesis-breaker read over their archived point-in-time news text, written to <outRoot>/news-risk/live/news-risk-{date}.{md,json} with every attempt durably persisted under <outRoot>/news-risk/assessments/ (run-radar.ps1 supplies Radar:NewsResearch:Shadow:OutputDirectory and DevelopmentExamplesPath). It changes NO score, label, rank or fingerprint; absence of a detected risk is never evidence of safety (fail-closed coverage/validation gates); and the BASELINE SHADOW SCHEDULES EXACTLY ONE READER: the hosted DeepInfra DeepSeek entry below. Note the semantics: a NON-EMPTY Readers list REPLACES the ambient Radar:Ai reader (it does not append to it), so that entry MUST be declared explicitly here or the baseline cohort silently vanishes — which is why the list is kept with one entry rather than deleted. Entry 0 re-declares the ambient DeepInfra DeepSeek (same BaseUrl/model/ApiKeyEnvVar as Radar:Ai — its cohort is model-scoped so it is continuous with the pre-Readers ambient cohort). SPEC 187 §8 (2026-08-24) - the second reader ('ollama-local', llama3.1), opted in on 2026-08-22 to test whether short pre-digested ARTICLE text is an easier read than accounting filings, is NO LONGER SCHEDULED in the baseline. This is a SCHEDULING decision, not a provider deletion: the Ollama IChatClient provider, its option binding, its provider tests and the ability of any -Profile overlay to declare it (for the shadow, or to point Radar:Ai back at it) are all retained; the accrued ollama:llama3.1 assessment/cohort data stays untouched as historical provenance and cohorts NEVER pool across providers/models; and Ollama is deliberately NOT substituted into the stage-1 typing or stage-2 judgment blocks below (spec 181 §1 measured 0.0% hosted vs 19.2% local citation-drop). No Claude CLI/provider/wrapper/cohort/fallback exists anywhere in Radar. So the baseline posture is now: shadow = ONE hosted DeepInfra DeepSeek reader; typing = ONE hosted DeepInfra DeepSeek reader; judgment = ONE hosted DeepInfra DeepSeek judge — one provider, one key (DEEPINFRA_API_KEY), one cohort per stage. EOSE/CASS/MSEX are declared development examples in docs/cohorts/news-risk-development.json and can never enter the evaluator's clean prospective table.
NewsResearch._comment2: Stage-1 news event typing (Radar:NewsResearch:Typing) and the stage-2 direction judge (Radar:NewsResearch:Judgment) run on every unfiltered full baseline run — promoted from the news-typing / news-judgment overlays by maintainer decision; those overlays remain as overlays. Both stages use the hosted DeepSeek reader ONLY (the local model failed the solo-typing gate measurement recorded in docs/architecture-history.md), so the baseline runs ONE hosted cohort per stage; the accrued local shadow cohort stays on disk as historical provenance and is never pooled with it. The judge reads ONLY canonical fact families and returns challenge-only findings plus the BusinessTrajectory axis; judgments are persisted beside the earlier shadow assessments — side by side, never pooled, no merged verdict. The weekly report's leaders rows carry the mandatory semantic-read marker fed by the PROSPECTIVELY designated PresentationCohort below (judge over extractor, declared before results and never switched after seeing them). That cohort IS a hashed ScoringConfigVersion input — its resolved cohort key sits in the news= segment (NewsJudgmentScoringIdentity) because the judgment-derived MediaAttention signal reaches scoring — so switching it is a scoring-identity move owned by ScoringConfigFingerprintTests; the typing budgets below are run provenance, never a judge input, and are not hashed. QUALITY CONTROL: the taxonomy revision mechanism (news-event-taxonomy-vN; cohorts never pool across versions) plus the per-run mechanical validation the pipeline records (citation-drop rate and reasons, ValidationFailed counts, per-cohort completeness) stand in for the row-by-row human audit, which was WAIVED by maintainer decision — revise the taxonomy when those numbers say so. BUDGETS: all five typing limits are declared EXPLICITLY here (MaxNewTypingsPerRun, LookbackDays, MaxTypingAttempts, MaxRetryTypingsPerRun, MaxCandidateTypingsPerRun) so an overlay cannot silently restore an older posture by inheriting a code default. The hosted typing calls per reader per run are split across three lanes: bounded FIFO retries (MaxRetryTypingsPerRun, oldest last-attempt first), then first attempts on the companies THIS run is about to judge (MaxCandidateTypingsPerRun, round-robin over the ONE shared candidate plan, so typing-prioritised == judged by construction), then every remaining slot on the global queue (window-new-first, then backlog oldest-first). The cross-field rule MaxCandidateTypingsPerRun + MaxRetryTypingsPerRun < MaxNewTypingsPerRun is enforced at startup so general first-attempt slots always remain and the legacy backlog keeps draining. Candidate coverage has a MOVING denominator (companies enter and leave the nominated set each run), so continuing candidate incompleteness ALONE is not evidence that the budget is too low. Every hosted typing call wins a DURABLE PRE-CALL reservation, so MaxTypingAttempts bounds provider CALLS, not persisted outcomes; judgment's attempt bound is separately DERIVED from durably recorded outcomes plus same-run idempotency and has NO pre-call ledger — accepted because judgment is one serial call per company per run while typing can spend hundreds. An exhausted company renders '? unassessed (retries-exhausted)' rather than a fabricated verdict; typing completeness distinguishes RetryableFailure from RetryExhausted (exhaustion takes precedence; legacy Failed stays readable, never newly computed). Nothing here auto-tunes: every posture is prospectively declared and then observed. The measured basis for the budgets, the falsifiable backlog-drain hypothesis and the per-spec narrative live in docs/architecture-history.md ('default.json _comment history', spec 213).

Comparison._comment: PairedFirstEligibleAsOfUtc is the spec-155 / AD-15 CLAIM BOUNDARY, and it is a PRECOMMITMENT, not a tuning knob. Declared 2026-08-03, when ZERO eligible outcomes existed, so it cannot have been derived from observed deltas — which is the entire reason it is worth anything. It deliberately reuses AD-16's first eligible primary-screen date (2026-09-29, itself pinned from PipelineRunRecord 7f28ca48 + 60 days) so the price-outcome and attention-outcome claim families share ONE calendar and spec 155's confirmatory layer lines up with the descriptive screen it sits behind. IMMUTABLE BY CONVENTION (spec 141's rule applied to a boundary): moving it invalidates the whole claim family, and moving it AFTER outcomes exist is the unfalsifiability failure AD-16's pre-commitment clause names — if a different boundary is ever genuinely needed, declare a new one prospectively and treat pre-boundary dates as development data. Dates before it still render, as development data that can never enter the claim interval. PairedPrimaryStrategy is the SECOND HALF of the same precommitment, declared in the same act on the same date and under the same rule: AD-15's amendment is explicit that naming whichever arm beats the baselines AFTER seeing results is selection, not evidence, so only the arm named here — before its outcomes exist — may ever use the gate. Every other configured arm stays exploratory until a separately accepted multiplicity rule exists. disclosure-led-v11 is chosen because it is ALREADY AD-16's precommitted primary arm (spec 157), so one hypothesis is judged against two independent outcomes (forward price here, publisher-count arrival there) on one shared calendar, rather than two arms being judged against two outcomes and the better pairing reported. RECORDED RISK, before any outcome exists: v11 is the youngest series (created 2026-07-28) and spec 158 measured its PREDECESSOR budget (form4 .50 / 13dg .30 / breadth .20) as a constant integer 0 across all 43 companies; the shipped budget is the measured option A (sec-edgar 1.00, S 3), but if it still yields a constant predictor those dates drop as ConstantPrimaryPredictor and the arm may simply fail to accrue six purged blocks. That is a real and acceptable way for this to end — a precommitment that cannot fail is not one — and it must NOT be repaired by swapping the primary later.

ReportedMetrics._comment: The earnings read keeps the metrics a release states, verified deterministically (ReportedMetricVerifier, policy token ReportedMetricsPolicy.Version) into an append-only ledger, so the judge can compare a quoted level against the company's own EARLIER figure; a reference is never the value the fact itself quotes (ReferenceValueProjector). Heal-forward. This flag shapes the filing-analysis prompt, so it IS a scoring-fingerprint input via the directional-filing descriptor's rm= field, owned by ScoringConfigFingerprintTests; a durable outbox (IReportedMetricOutbox) retries a failed ledger write rather than losing it.
